subject: EmberPay performance gate & onboarding evidence workflow
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@emberpay.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@emberpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-20T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: EmberPay onboarding: proposed performance gate workflow and data requests

Hi Sanjay / Elena,

Thanks again for the productive kickoff yesterday. To keep the onboarding timeline tight and avoid surprises during the go/no-go, I put together a short performance gate workflow and the immediate artifacts we need from your side to run the first acceptance pass. High level: we run a week of smoke load tests (concurrency sweep + steady-state), collect latency percentiles and error rates, then validate against the agreed gates.

Key targets (proposed):
- 95th latency under 220ms for 512-token avg requests at 50 RPS steady state
- p99 tail under 480ms during steady-state bursts
- End-to-end success >= 99.5% (no request errors attributable to inference runtime)
- Throughput acceptance: sustained 3k tokens/sec on the configured dedicated pool during baseline run

Immediate asks from EmberPay (please share by Tue 2028-05-23):
1) Representative load profile CSV (sample attached format) with per-endpoint request mix and average token lengths.
2) Any traffic shaping rules, auth headers, or IP allowlist we need to configure.
3) A test API key or short-lived token and a contact for infra coordination (InfraOps ok).

Plan overview:
- Mon 5/24: Baseline single-instance latency sweep (low concurrency)
- Tue–Thu 5/25–5/26: Concurrency ramp + steady-state runs and burst windows
- Fri 5/27: Evidence export, dashboard readout, and decision (go / tweak / backlog)

I'll lead the test orchestration, Monica will own telemetry collection and artifacts, and Priya will handle model variant knobs and quantization checks. Ben, looping you for any license or dedicated pool setup blockers.

I'll attach the CSV template and a short checklist to make it easier to populate. If these gates look off to you, flag them and we'll adjust — want conservatively realistic targets but not impossible.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Attachments referenced: emberpay-load-profile.csv (template), redwood-onboard-checklist.xlsx
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@emberpay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@emberpay.com>, InfraOps <infraops@emberpay.com>
Date: 2028-05-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EmberPay onboarding: proposed performance gate workflow and data requests

Marcus — thanks for the clear plan. We're aligned on timeline and the targets look achievable as long as the request mix is what we've been seeing internally. Quick notes:

- Uploading our representative load profile (attached) — includes endpoint-level mix and token histograms.
- InfraOps will provide a short-lived test API token and coordinate IP allowlist by EOD Monday.
- One caveat: our production prompts include a small percentage of long-system messages (~3% > 1k tokens). We can flag those during runs and exclude from baseline if needed, or run a capped-long request window.

We'll review the CSV template and send the completed file by 5/23.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform, EmberPay
sanjay.rao@emberpay.com

Attachments: emberpay-load-profile.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@emberpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-23T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EmberPay onboarding: proposed performance gate workflow and data requests

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the heads up on long requests — good to know. A couple follow-ups:

- We'll run an exclusion window for long messages during baseline and a separate long-tail run to show impact. Please label long-response endpoints in the CSV so we can script exclusions easily.
- Ben — can you confirm whether a dedicated 1-node pool (NVIDIA A100 equivalent) is provisioned under EPD-421 or if we should use burst capacity? We want to avoid CPU-side fanouts affecting tail latency.
- Monica / Priya, I'll hand off orchestration notes tomorrow AM; expect a short meeting invite for 5/24 09:30 PT to kick off the baseline.

Next steps for EmberPay: attach the filled CSV and a preferred contact for any test failures (pager / slack channel).

Marcus
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@emberpay.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-24T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Operational handoff: telemetry, evidence artifacts, and sign-off checklist

Hi team — following Marcus's orchestration, here's the operational handoff doc in email form so everyone has the same checklist during the runs. We'll collect artifacts into a single folder and circulate the evidence export before Friday's readout.

Telemetry we'll capture (automated):
- Per-request latency buckets (p50/p95/p99) per endpoint and per model variant
- Token throughput per second and per minute aggregates
- Error codes with stack traces when available (inference runtime vs application)
- Resource utilization (GPU % active, host CPU, GPU memory) sampled at 10s intervals

Artifacts for acceptance package (we'll assemble):
1) CSV: run-level summary with request mix and token counts
2) PDF: latency percentile plots and tail heatmap (aggregate and per-endpoint)
3) JSON: raw samples for any failed requests for post-mortem
4) XLSX: acceptance checklist with gate pass/fail and comments

Sign-off criteria (formal):
- Dev lead (EmberPay) acknowledges dataset representativeness
- Redwood: telemetry matches expected collection, gates evaluated per checklist
- Joint decision: Go if gates pass; Partial go for tweaks; Hold if p99 > gate and root cause in model or infra

I've created the evidence folder and a Drive link (see related_links). After each run we'll drop the artifacts and leave a one-line status in the readme: PASS / FAIL / TUNED.

If we hit unexpected infra errors (5xx) > 0.5% we'll pause and engage InfraOps.

I'll run the baseline orchestration now — Marcus, Sanjay, expect the initial telemetry snapshot in ~35 minutes.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@emberpay.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-27T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EmberPay performance gate & onboarding evidence workflow — evidence export and next steps

Quick readout from today's evidence export attached. Summary: baseline and steady-state runs completed; we observed the following:

- Baseline (low concurrency): p95 = 180ms, p99 = 360ms — within gates
- Steady-state 50 RPS: p95 = 210ms, p99 = 465ms — within gates but close to tail target during the midday burst window
- Error rate: 0.12% end-to-end, root-caused to a malformed request on one endpoint (sample attached)
- Throughput: 3.1k tokens/sec sustained during baseline dedicated pool run

Artifacts uploaded to Drive (see link): latency-results-20280520.pdf, raw-failures.json, run-summary.csv. Monica has filled the acceptance checklist and marked baseline as PASS with notes on a small follow-up to harden a parsing edge-case.

Next steps:
- EmberPay infra to verify the malformed-request pattern and push a small fix (target EOD 5/29).
- We'll schedule a short review on Mon 5/30 to confirm patch and finalize sign-off.
- Ben: confirm billing for the dedicated node under EPD-421 and convert burst capacity if needed.

If everyone is comfortable with the artifacts I'll draft the formal go/no-go email to the exec sponsors after the Mon check.

Thanks all — good progress.

Marcus Lin
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: latency-results-20280520.pdf, run-summary.csv
